Thursday
May 2, 1935.
Dear Tamily:
I am writing this letter en route from Canton northward.
left Canton at 6:45 årl, and now at 7:05 we are flying at 3000 feet over
the rich delta lands of
the Pearl River.
le are climbing all the time
for ahead is a four thousand foot high mountain range which we must
cross in order to reach the coast near famous,
or rather infamous,
Bias Bay, north of hongkong.
Bias Bay is the
breeding ground and
headquarters for Chinese pirates.
The bay is too shallow for Chinese
aruisers to enter in pursuit of pirate junks and if smaller craft chase
the pirates into the bay a they sre apt to be set upon by the armored
Junks and may come off second best.
Flew down to Canton on Monday with five members of the American
Economic Mission.
The Chairman of the Mission is the Hon. #. Cameron
Forbes, formerly Governor General of the Philippines.
His grandfather
came to Canton 105 years ago and organized the firm of Russell & Co.
which was a most successful American trading concern.
The old Clipper
shipe of Russell & Company carried silk and tea to Boston and I suspect
the firm also did a considerable volume in opium as most of the other
treders did in those early days. le spent two busy daya at Canton with
every minute taken up by parties, sightseeing and official calls.
is a strange thing thet in China the most energetic progressive and
adventurious people live in the south, while the northerners are more
or less content with things as they are and ever have been.
in Canton I met General Art Lim of the Canton air fore whi
s an old time pilot who learned to fly before the orld war.
one of the early "crates" to Canton and made a number of flights before
he cracked up.
One amusing story which is told about him relates how
the sailors on the three Cantonese battleships mutinied and started
down river for the open sea.
Art Lim was offered $1000 to attack the
He had no aerial
bombs so he rilled sone quart whiskey bottles
with high test gas and steel nails. THe then dove his plane close to the
fleeing warships and hurled the bottles on the decks - the breaking
bottles, sparking nails and gasoline set fire to the ships and seared
the mutineers so badly that they all jumped over board or surrendered.
Art flew triumphantly baok to the airport where a large crowd had
gathered, removed hia helmet and goggles to acknowledge the plaudits of
the crowd, whereupon according to the story, his eyes filled with tears
and he couldn't see some trees on the edge
of the field. At any rate he
spent several months in the hospital.
We landed at Swatow and then again at Amoy where
we picked up 3 Chinese passengers for Foochow.
These passengers had
been eating garlio and the cabin soon filled up with such a stench that
I almost became physically i11, As a matter of fact one of the Chinese
became airsick and that delicate odor was a delightful antidote for the
garlic. Fortunately the garlio gentry only rode to Foochow and now I
can go on with my letter,
le, Chevalier of the american Mission and
I are traveling back to Shanghei on the reguler scheduled plane. The
other members are leaving by special plane from Canton & noon and will
stay over night at Foochow.
on saturday the entire party will fly to
Tsingtao staying there until Monday and then continue on to Tientsin
for a few days and then to Peiping.
by rail to Hankow and then up the river to Chungking by air.
expeot to
stay with them most of the time but will have to get away one in awhile
so as to keep up with developments and business at Shanghai.
Debby and all the girle are going to Feiping on May 4th and
stay there while I am traveling around with the Mission.
As Evrr
Haraci
